column1: # Hand-placed VAC panels, for plates the graticule reader cannot do.
# One line per panel, tab or space separated:
#   ident  section  page  x0 y0 x1 y1  latSW lonSW  latNE lonNE
# The clip is in PDF points with the origin at the bottom left, which is
# what `go run ./cmd/vacgeo -only <ident> -dump` prints and what
# `pdftoppm -x -y -W -H` crops with. The two corners are decimal degrees,
# negative west and south.
# An override is gated exactly like a fit: the aerodrome has to fall inside
# the panel. A typed control point is at least as easy to get wrong as a
# misread label.
# Every entry carries the reason it is here.
# LFPN PARIS SACLAY VERSAILLES, landing sheet, AD-2 plate page 2.
# The page carries two map panels and the automatic reader placed neither.
# Its graticule is a clean one-minute comb, nine meridian ticks along the
# bottom neatline and four parallel ticks down the left one, but the labels
# name every FOURTH tick and the corner label is pushed inboard to stay
# inside the frame, so no label sits on the tick it names. The runway
# fallback then fitted the runways drawn in the SECOND panel, the aerodrome
# diagram lower down the same page, against a frame enclosing both: the
# second runway landed 139.9 m out and the sheet would have put the ARP
# 1225 m from where the plate prints it, which is what runway:cross refused.
# Measured off the ticks at 600 dpi: 41.055 pt per minute of longitude from
# 002 02' at x 18.78, 62.08 pt per minute of latitude from 48 45' at 100.02
# from the page top. Checked three ways, none of them the fit: the two axes
# stand in 1.5123 where sec(48.75) is 1.5173; the printed scale bar reads
# 33.4 pt per km against the 33.6 the longitude comb gives; and both
# published runways, projected through this mapping, lie on the two drawn
# strips for 59 of 61 centreline samples with clear paper 120 m past every
# threshold.
LFPN
# The seven the reader still cannot tie, 2026-09 cycle.
# Each prints a graticule and the reader finds it; what it cannot do is put
# the labels on the ticks. Reims and Compiegne label every SECOND tick and
# their combs run at 30-second intervals, which niceSteps has no entry for by
# decision (adding one was measured once and cost ten panels for seven);
# Chavenay, Lyon-Bron and Etain carry two map panels on one page and only the
# upper one is a landing chart; Enghien, Luchon and Salon label their corners
# inboard, off the line their own family sits on.
# All seven were measured the same way: the tick comb read off a 600 dpi
# render, the labels supplying only which arcminute each tick IS (they wander
# a couple of points against it), and the clip taken just inside the map's own
# neatlines. The columns are the two axes in points per arcminute with the
# number of labels each was tied by, the panel's axis ratio against
# axisRatio() at its own latitude, and the worst distance from a PUBLISHED
# runway end, projected through the typed mapping, to the ink the plate draws
# there. That last one owes nothing to the graticule and is what each entry
# stands on.
#   ident  sheet          lon pt/'     lat pt/'     ratio vs axisRatio   worst end
# Enghien's is the strongest of them and the one to read first: its approach
# sheet covers the whole north of Paris, so the check lands the runway ends of
# CDG, Le Bourget and Persan as well as its own, eleven runways on their own
# drawn strips.
# A FOURTH check, since one exists now: each panel measured against IGN's own
# survey through its own drawn line work. Three of the eight read far enough
# out to be worth looking at, Chavenay 119.2 m, Lyon-Bron 66.0 and
# Reims-Prunay 48.4, every one of them on five windows of five. All three
# were then opened over orthophotos and all three draw their RUNWAY on the
# real runway. What the measurement sees is the plate's background, which a
# VAC chart draws approximately where it draws its runway from the survey
# (docs/fr-vacgeo.md, "The witness"). The typed coordinates stand.
#   ident  sheet            worst end   against the ground
#   LFQA   Reims-Prunay       2.6 pt     48.4 m, 4.3 pt, 5 of 5 windows
#   LFPX   Chavenay           1.5 pt    119.2 m, 5.9 pt, 5 of 5
#   LFLY   Lyon-Bron          2.0 pt     66.0 m, 3.7 pt, 5 of 5
#   LFQE   Etain-Rouvres      0.8 pt     31.6 m, 3.0 pt, 2 of 2
#   LFFE   Enghien            1.8 pt     52.1 m, 0.6 pt, 2 of 5
#   LFCB   Luchon             2.3 pt    343.2 m, 3.9 pt, 2 of 5
#   LFNE   Salon-Eyguieres    1.5 pt     22.3 m, 0.6 pt, 2 of 5
#   LFPN   Toussus            (above)    51.2 m, 1.7 pt, 4 of 5
LFQA
